newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: South Africa eyes seven-year mark bond maturity.
newsitem.headline: South Africa eyes seven-year mark bond maturity.

text.p: South Africa was considering a maturity of about seven years for its proposed Euromark bond issue, the director-general of South Africa's Finance Department Maria Ramos said on Wednesday.
She said the South African government would be guided by the market on the preferred size and coupon for the issue, which is lead managed by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Morgan Stanley.

"One of the objectives of our foreign debt strategy is to extend the maturity profile of our foreign debt. As a result we are looking at something in the seven year region," Ramos told a news conference.
She is part of a delegation of South African officials visiting European financial centres this week to re-establish relationships with financial institutions and markets.
Ramos said the officials would talk to investors about the issue and make a decision on Friday about the best terms for the bond issue.
Asked when the bond would be issued, she said: "We will probably look at doing something shortly after that."
She said although a South African 400 million mark bond would mature next month, the new bond was seen as a means of funding the budget deficit rather than a refinancing.
Foreign borrowings represent only 4.2 percent of South African central government debt.
Only 2.5 billion rand of the forecast 1996/97 borrowing requirement of more than 40 billion rand is scheduled to be raised offshore.
Ramos said South Africa had no problem funding its deficit domestically, but it wanted to raise funds overseas to improve and re-establish its bonds as benchmarks in foreign markets.
The country, which returned to the international capital markets in 1994 after years of isolation during the apartheid era, has also issued in yen, sterling and dollars.
Finance Minister Trevor Manuel declined to comment on market speculation South Africa planned a Yankee bond in October.
"We will leave it to speculation until such time as a decision is taken," he told the news conference.
He also said a Dutch guilder bond issue was not "on the horizon" in the 1996/97 fiscal year.
